observations: The neutral shell, Radix colors, typography, hairline borders, restrained radii and field rows are reflected in apps/dashboard/src/lib/styles/tokens.css, radix.css and the Svelte UI components.
limitations: The email uses a token subset and inline styles with email-safe font fallbacks. It reproduces the relevant patterns without the application stylesheet, which email clients cannot load.

observations: The mailbox is confirmed once per account: POST /api/internal/account/weekly-report/confirmation emails a link {base}/weekly-report/confirm/{token} (43-character base64url token, valid 1 hour, single use, only its SHA-256 hash stored; a new request invalidates the earlier link; one request per account per minute, 429 with Retry-After). The confirmation email is plain text: subject 确认接收 Rivu 周报 / Confirm your email for Rivu weekly reports, one explanatory sentence, the link, and an ignore line, with no unsubscribe line or header. Opening the link only checks it (GET /api/weekly-report/confirm/{token}); POST confirms. Every failure of the token is the same 404. Request returns 503 mail_unavailable without SMTP and 502 mail_failed when SMTP refuses it.

Reports cover the previous complete site-local week and are sent after 09:00 on the site's first weekday. The body carries the site name, ISO from/to dates, time zone, visitors, visits, pageviews, {base}/s/{site_id} and a last line Unsubscribe: {base}/api/weekly-report/unsubscribe/{token} (Chinese 退订周报：). {base} is RIVU_BASE_URL without trailing slashes. Subjects are fixed per language. The report body and subjects are unchanged by the account-level confirmation.

Each claimed send record gets a new 43-character base64url token; only its SHA-256 hash is stored with the user, the site and the confirmation time of the subscription. GET /api/weekly-report/unsubscribe/{token} returns a confirmation page and changes nothing; POST deletes the subscription of that one site while the confirmation time still matches, and otherwise returns the expired-or-already-off page. The confirmed mailbox and other sites are untouched. A malformed token is 404. The pages are fixed bilingual HTML, no cookie or session, with Content-Security-Policy default-src 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none', plus no-store and no-referrer.
inferences: A confirmation email needs only the link, a validity line and an ignore line; it has no site to name because the confirmation belongs to the account.
limitations: The API does not return the stored email language, the next send date or the confirmation time.
The unsubscribe pages ignore the email language and the CSP rules out styles, scripts and images, so they stay unstyled unless the response policy changes.

The HTML versions of the emails do not exist in production; the plain-text emails, the account page, the confirmation page and the unsubscribe pages do. The subscription UI prototype is in designs/rivu-svelte, not in this directory.

observations: remove_member deletes the member's weekly report subscriptions for the organization's sites unless a site guest membership remains. remove_guest deletes the guest's subscription for that site unless an organization membership remains. Send records are kept.
inferences: A user who lost access loses the site's subscription, and it does not come back with the access.
limitations: A disabled or deleted account is not cleaned up by these two functions; the sender skips such accounts when it picks recipients.

observations: Mailer::message builds multipart/alternative (plain text first, HTML second) when Mail.html is set, which the two weekly report emails do; invitations and password resets stay text/plain. When Mail.unsubscribe_url is set (weekly reports only) the message gets List-Unsubscribe: <url> and List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click; the confirmation email, the invitation and the password reset do not set it.
inferences: The HTML and plain-text parts are built in crates/mail/src/weekly_report.rs from the same data, so both carry the same links.
limitations: Rendering was checked in Chromium only, not in real mail clients.

observations: The primary variant uses --accent-solid with --accent-contrast text. The emails' button uses the same solid blue as an inline background.
